_comment: Known sub-44px controls on AUTHENTICATED phone screens, measured by
authed-phone.spec.ts in the `mobile-auth` lane. Same contract and same
ratchet semantics as undersized-target-baseline.json: the spec fails on
anything NOT listed here, so this file can only shrink.
IT IS A SEPARATE FILE ON PURPOSE, AND THE REASON IS A TEST THAT CAUGHT ME.
The public baseline is pinned by target-ratchet.test.ts to cover EXACTLY the
routes the smoke spec visits — no more, no less — because a route present in
one and absent from the other either turns every known control into a
regression or hides them all. Adding /core/trades to that file broke the
assertion immediately, which is the invariant working. Relaxing it to a union
of two specs' routes would have weakened a check that does real work in order
to accommodate a new lane; a second file keeps it exact.
The two lanes also have different lifecycles. `mobile-smoke` gates every PR;
`mobile-auth` is new, is not a required context, and is expected to churn
while authenticated screens get measured for the first time. Mixing their
debt into one file would make neither readable.
/core/trades STARTS EMPTY because nothing has ever rendered it at 390px.
`/core/*` redirects to /login without a session and to /import without a
league, so every mobile check this repo had stopped at the marketing routes.
A red first run is debt being surfaced for the first time, not a regression
anyone introduced — baseline what it finds deliberately, one entry at a time,
and only where the control is genuinely pre-existing debt being deferred.
⚠ Trade Center's four primary actions were sized by CSS specificity, not by
this file: `.af-tc-actions .af-btn` was (0,2,0), dead equal to
`.af-core .af-btn { min-height: 36px }`, so 44px applied on a coin toss
decided by stylesheet order. Fixed by prefixing with `.af-core`. If entries
appear here for `.af-btn` controls, check the specificity before baselining —
a losing rule looks exactly like a missing one.
WHAT THE FIRST RUNS FOUND, AND WHY ONLY THE DOTS ARE HERE. /core/trades came
back with three undersized shell controls and three sub-16px fields. Two were
FIXED rather than baselined, because both were mechanical: .af-search-input at
13px (iOS Safari zooms on focus and never back out) and .af-nav-support at 36px
tall, 8px short of a floor the rest of /core already holds. Only the help dots
are deferred, and only because reaching 44px there changes the design rather
than the stylesheet. Baseline what you cannot fix mechanically; fix the rest.
WHAT /core FOUND WHEN IT WAS ADDED (2026-09-19), AND WHY IT ADDED NO NEW DEBT.
The home screen measured at 390px reported exactly two undersized controls, and
both are the help dots already deferred above -- they live in AfCoreShell's
topbar, so they are on every /core screen and a second route was always going to
re-report them. Nothing else: the premise guard held, there was no sideways
overflow, and ZERO sub-16px fields.
⚠ AND THE POSITIVE CONTROL FOR THIS ROUTE DID NOT REPRODUCE, WHICH IS WHY THIS
PARAGRAPH REPLACED THE ONE THAT CLAIMED IT WOULD. The first draft asserted that
removing af-core.css's shell-wide iOS zoom floor would make /core report
.af3a-search-input at 13px. Measured by doing exactly that -- floor stripped,
mutation asserted applied, database reset, route re-run -- and /core PASSED.
The field is in the DOM and is not visible on this route: Dashboard3A ships its
own topbar for a standalone render, and af-core-shell.css:822 sets
`.af-content .af3a-topbar { display: none }` so the embedded copy does not
double the shell's chrome. CoreHomeCards is rendered only from
app/core/[[...screen]]/page.tsx, always inside .af-content, so that input is not
reachable anywhere in the product today. The probe is right to skip it.
WHAT TO TAKE FROM THAT: this route certifies a screen rather than rescuing one,
and a claim about what a gate CATCHES is worth nothing until the gate has been
seen to catch it. The control cost one run and stopped a false sentence from
becoming the permanent record here.
WHAT /core/my-team FOUND (2026-09-19), AND WHY ONLY THE DOTS ARE HERE. Four
undersized controls: the two shell help dots above, plus .af-welcome-close at
36x36 and .af-welcome-next at 42 tall. Both welcome-tour buttons were FIXED in
core-welcome-tour.css rather than baselined -- they were already deliberate
touch-target boxes a few pixels short of the floor, which is the same shape as
.af-nav-support and the same reason it was fixed. The close button is the only
way to dismiss the tour, so a 36px hit area was the worst place to be short.
⚠ THIS ROUTE IS LEAGUE-SCOPED AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. /core/my-team renders
the roster only with a league in context; without one it renders the
cross-league picker at the SAME pathname, so the premise guard cannot tell
them apart and the picker passes every measurement. authedRoutes marks it
leagueScoped, and the spec asserts .af-mt present AND .af-pl absent -- both
directions, because asserting only the roster would still pass if a layout
ever rendered both.
WHAT SCOPING matchup AND trades FOUND (2026-09-20), AND THE SURPRISE IN IT.
Both now render their real screens: matchup .af-mu at 200 af elements, Trade
Center .af-tc at 316. matchup reported only the two shell help dots -- no new
debt.
🛑 AND /core/trades HAD NEVER MEASURED TRADE CENTER UNTIL NOW. It carried no
root selector, so with no league in context it rendered the no-league screen:
205 af elements in every CI run to date, against 316 for the real thing. The
description of this route as Trade Center coverage was wrong for its whole
life. Its baseline did NOT move when the real screen was finally measured --
the same two help dots -- which is luck rather than vindication.
⚠ BOTH ROUTES WERE DROPPED ONCE BEFORE AS NONDETERMINISTIC, AND THE CAUSE WAS
REAL. They fell back to the picker whenever their loader threw, silently. That
is fixed at the source: a failed read now renders ScreenLoadError and logs
`[core/<screen>] read failed`. If one of these routes goes red with NEITHER the
screen nor the picker present, read that line -- it names the cause instead of
leaving a shrug.

/core.label: Read-only by design
/core.why: THE SAME TWO SHELL CONTROLS ALREADY DEFERRED ON /core/trades, not new debt. They live in AfCoreShell's topbar, so they are on EVERY /core screen; measuring a second route was always going to re-report them. Deferred for the reason recorded below: a 15x15 info dot cannot reach 44x44 by min-height, it needs an expanded hit area that shifts layout around a deliberately small affordance. Retire both routes' entries together when the shell's help affordances are next touched.

/core.why: Same control, second instance. See above.

/core/trades.label: Read-only by design
/core/trades.why: DEFERRED DESIGN WORK, NOT A SIZING OVERSIGHT. A 15x15 info dot cannot reach 44x44 by min-height: it needs an expanded hit area (a pseudo-element or padding that does not move the dot), which shifts layout around a deliberately small affordance. That is a design decision, not a CSS one. Sized alongside its sibling below when the shell's help affordances are next touched.

/core/trades.why: Same control, second instance. See above.
